name: Quotient group criterion
statement: If N is a normal subgroup of G, then the set of left cosets G/N forms a group under (aN)(bN) = abN.
conditions: N is a subgroup of G
conclusion: G/N is a group and coset multiplication is well-defined.
typical_uses: prove induced maps to quotient groups
common_misuses: forming G/N when N is not known to be normal
assuming coset multiplication is well-defined without checking normality

name: Kernel is normal
statement: If phi: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then ker(phi) is a normal subgroup of G.
conditions: phi is a group homomorphism from G to H
common_misuses: assuming the preimage of an arbitrary subset is normal
using normality of the image instead of the kernel

name: First isomorphism theorem for groups
statement: If phi: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).
conditions: ker(phi) is the kernel of phi
typical_uses: prove a quotient is isomorphic to an image
common_misuses: quotienting by a subgroup that is not the kernel
claiming G is isomorphic to H without surjectivity

name: Lagrange theorem
statement: If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup of G, then |H| divides |G|.
conditions: H is a subgroup of G
typical_uses: prove element order divides group order
common_misuses: using the theorem for infinite groups
assuming every divisor gives a subgroup

name: Subgroup test
statement: A nonempty subset H of a group G is a subgroup if for all a,b in H, ab^{-1} is in H.
conditions: H is a subset of G
conclusion: H is a subgroup of G.
typical_uses: prove a subset is a subgroup
common_misuses: checking closure under product but not inverses

name: Quotient ring criterion
statement: If I is a two-sided ideal of a ring R, then R/I is a quotient ring with operations defined on cosets.
conditions: I is a two-sided ideal of R
conclusion: R/I is a ring and coset operations are well-defined.
common_misuses: quotienting by a subset that is not an ideal
using a one-sided ideal when a two-sided ideal is required

name: Kernel is an ideal
statement: If phi: R -> S is a ring homomorphism, then ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
conditions: phi is a ring homomorphism from R to S
conclusion: ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
typical_uses: apply the first isomorphism theorem for rings
common_misuses: assuming the image is an ideal
using a non-homomorphism to define a kernel ideal

name: Rank-nullity theorem
statement: If T: V -> W is linear and V is finite-dimensional, then dim V = dim ker(T) + dim im(T).
conclusion: dim V = dim ker(T) + dim im(T).
typical_uses: relate injectivity, surjectivity, rank, and nullity
prove injective iff surjective for endomorphisms of finite-dimensional spaces
common_misuses: concluding im(T) = W from equal dimensions without im(T) being a subspace of W

name: Same dimension subspace criterion
statement: If W is a subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space V and dim W = dim V, then W = V.
conditions: W is a subspace of V
typical_uses: identify a subspace with the whole space
common_misuses: using dimension equality without a subspace relation
using the criterion in infinite-dimensional settings
